dm.story_so_far: The Whistlers walked out onto the Gullhaven flats at dusk as the fog came in. Ada found a psalm stamped on every seventh link of the ferry chain ('Bear me over, ferryman, for I have no coin'), and the last line was half filed away. Bram followed the bare footprints to the channel edge, where the last prints sink deeper at the toe, as if the walker was lifted. Dev heard that the bell is a replayed ring with a man's voice under it counting coins to forty. Cass's boot sucked out of the mud, and the thing in the fog turned and tasted her (a Bleed mark, held for Death Defy). It reached for her along the chain and missed. The circle crossed by the chain to the far bank and reached the ferryman's cottage, shut these forty years. Inside are a psalm sheet whose handwriting changes halfway down, a tide-ledger with a swollen brass lock, and a portrait of the ferryman (the dispatch names him Absalom Hode, drowned 1886) with the face scratched out. Something wet is trying the latch.
